mainTopic: לוט's split from אברהם, the power of intention (תמר, זמרי, יעל), the value of מצוות שלא לשמה (בלק and רות), and reward for refined speech and for being first to do a מצוה
overview: This amud continues the discussion of לוט and his daughters. First, two פסוקים in משלי are read as describing לוט: he split from אברהם to chase his desires. Because of this, his descendants עמון and מואב are banned from the קהל forever, and his shame is still talked about in shuls and study halls. Next, עולא contrasts תמר and זמרי. Both did a forbidden act, but תמר's was for a מצוה and brought kings and prophets, while זמרי's brought death to thousands. רב נחמן בר יצחק turns this into a rule about an עבירה לשמה. After a challenge from רב's teaching, the rule is softened to 'equal to a מצוה שלא לשמה,' and it is proven from יעל. The גמרא then goes back to רב's teaching that one should do מצוות even שלא לשמה, proving it from בלק, whose קרבנות earned him רות as a descendant. Finally, it shows how ה׳ rewarded לוט's daughters for their modest speech and for hurrying to do a מצוה, a teaching that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: לוט is the offended brother who locked the gates
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes explaining משלי 18:19. The 'offended brother' is לוט, who split from אברהם. The 'bars of a castle' are the permanent barrier he caused: עמוני and מואבי may not enter the קהל.
steps.simpleTranslation: [What is the meaning of the verse: 'A brother offended is harder to win than a strong city,] and their quarrels are like the bars of a castle'? 'A brother offended' is לוט, who separated from אברהם. 'Their quarrels are like the bars of a castle' means that he brought quarrels that are like the bars and locks of a castle, as it says: 'An עמוני and a מואבי shall not enter the congregation of ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a explanation of a פסוק in משלי, showing that it is talking about לוט and the result of his leaving אברהם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק has two halves. The first half names the person: לוט, the 'brother' who broke away. The second half describes the result: just as bars lock a castle so nobody can get in, לוט's descendants are locked out of the Jewish people forever.

keyTerms.meaning: An offended or estranged brother; here, לוט
A bar or bolt that locks a gate

steps.confusionAlert: The step begins in the middle of the question. The opening words, 'What is the meaning of the verse, a brother offended is harder to win than a strong city', come just before this section.

phrases.english: "and their quarrels are like the bars of a castle"?
phrases.notes: This is the end of a question about משלי 18:19. The first half of the פסוק was quoted just before this.

phrases.english: "A brother offended is harder to win than a strong city"
This is Lot, who separated from Abraham.
"And their quarrels are like the bars of a castle"
that he brought quarrels like bars and a castle,
"An Ammonite and a Moabite shall not enter the congregation of the Lord."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָח נִפְשָׁע מִקִּרְיַת עֹז זֶה לוֹט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion of לוט from just before this section, completing the explanation of משלי 18:19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משלי 18:19 refers to לוט: his split from אברהם caused a permanent barrier, since עמוני and מואבי may not enter the קהל.

steps.title: Lot followed his desires, and his shame is still discussed
steps.stepSummary: רבא (or רבי יצחק) explains משלי 18:1 as being about לוט. He left אברהם to chase his desires, and as a result his disgrace is 'revealed' in shuls and study halls.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא taught, and some say it was רבי יצחק: What is the meaning of the verse: 'He who separates himself seeks his own desire, and snarls against all sound wisdom'? 'He who separates himself seeks his own desire' is לוט. 'And snarls [יתגלע] against all sound wisdom' means that his shame was revealed [נתגלה] in the shuls and in the study halls.
steps.whatsHappening: A second teacher explains another פסוק in משלי in the same way, again showing that it is about לוט leaving אברהם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the פסוק describes why לוט left: he was chasing his desires, since he chose the rich land of סדום. The second half is read through a play on words. 'יתגלע' sounds like 'נתגלה', revealed. So the פסוק is hinting that לוט's shame would become public: his story is read aloud in shul, and the הלכות of his descendants are studied in the בית מדרש.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (it was said by someone else)
Snarls or breaks out; read here as 'revealed'

phrases.english: Rava expounded, and some say it was Rabbi Yitzchak:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"He who separates himself seeks his own desire,
and snarls against all sound wisdom"?
"He who separates himself seeks his own desire" — this is Lot,
"and snarls against all sound wisdom" —
that his shame was revealed
phrases.notes: This is a play on words: יִתְגַּלָּע sounds like נִתְגַּלָּה, which means 'was revealed.'

phrases.english: in the synagogues and in the study halls.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵשׁ רָבָא וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי יִצְחָק מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel explanation of a different פסוק in משלי, also applied to לוט's separation from אברהם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משלי 18:1 refers to לוט: he left in pursuit of his desires, and his shame is publicized in shuls and study halls.

steps.title: Proof from a משנה: the ban is forever
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה that says עמוני and מואבי are forbidden forever. This shows that לוט's shame is discussed in the study halls.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: An עמוני and a מואבי are forbidden, and their prohibition is a permanent one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the last step by quoting a משנה. This shows exactly what is taught about לוט's descendants in the בית מדרש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous step said לוט's shame is revealed 'in the study halls.' This משנה is the example. Every time people learn the הלכה that עמוני and מואבי may never marry into the קהל, the result of לוט's choices is discussed again.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
A man from עמון or מואב, the descendants of לוט
A permanent prohibition, lasting for all generations

steps.whatToRemember: Both פסוקים in משלי are read as being about לוט. His split from אברהם led to a permanent ban on עמוני and מואבי, and this ban keeps his shame publicly remembered.

phrases.english: As we learned: An Ammonite and a Moabite are prohibited,
phrases.notes: This means they may never marry into the Jewish people.

phrases.english: and their prohibition is a permanent prohibition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 2's claim that לוט's shame is revealed in the study halls.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that לוט's disgrace is publicized in the בית מדרש.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה ruling that עמוני and מואבי are forbidden permanently.

steps.title: עולא: same act, opposite results for תמר and זמרי
steps.stepSummary: עולא points out that תמר and זמרי both did an act of זנות. תמר, who acted for a מצוה, became the ancestor of kings and prophets. Because of זמרי, who acted for sin, many thousands of Jews died.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: תמר committed זנות, and זמרי committed זנות. תמר committed זנות, and kings and prophets came from her. זמרי committed זנות, and many tens of thousands of Jews fell because of him.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא compares two people who did a similar act and shows that their results were completely opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא first sets up the two cases side by side so they look the same. Then he reveals the different outcomes. תמר acted to have children from יהודה's family, for the sake of a מצוה, and דוד's royal line came from her. זמרי acted out of lust and rebellion, and a plague followed. This fits the earlier discussion of לוט's daughters: what a person intends can change the whole meaning of an act.

keyTerms.meaning: Committed זנות, a forbidden relationship (feminine / masculine form)
The daughter-in-law of יהודה, who had children from him (בראשית 38)
זמרי בן סלוא, who sinned with a Midianite woman (במדבר 25)

steps.whatToRemember: The same outward act can have opposite results depending on the reason behind it. תמר acted for a מצוה and was blessed with kings and prophets, while זמרי's sin brought death to many.
steps.confusionAlert: עולא is not praising זנות. His point is only that תמר's intention was for a מצוה, so her outcome was blessed, while זמרי's was for sin.

phrases.english: Ulla said:
Tamar committed licentiousness, Zimri committed licentiousness.
Tamar committed licentiousness —
kings and prophets descended from her.
Zimri committed licentiousness —
several tens of thousands of Israel fell on his account.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא תָּמָר זִינְּתָה זִמְרִי זִינָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching, connected to the earlier discussion of לוט's daughters, about how intention changes the outcome of an act.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An act done for the sake of a מצוה (תמר) brings blessing, while the same kind of act done for sin (זמרי) brings disaster.

steps.title: A sin for Heaven is greater than a מצוה not for its own sake
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק teaches that an עבירה לשמה is greater than a מצוה שלא לשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: A sin done for the sake of Heaven is greater than a מצוה done not for its own sake.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק makes a bold statement about the value of intention: a sin done for the right reason is greater than a מצוה done for the wrong reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds on עולא's point about תמר, whose forbidden act was for a good purpose and brought great results. רב נחמן בר יצחק turns it into a general rule that intention can outweigh the act itself. The next step will challenge how far this goes.

keyTerms.meaning: A sin done for the sake of Heaven, with a pure goal
A מצוה done for a personal motive, not purely for Heaven

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Greater is a sin done for its own sake
phrases.notes: 'For its own sake' here means for the sake of Heaven, with a good purpose.

phrases.english: than a מצוה done not for its own sake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns עולא's תמר and זמרי contrast into a general rule about intention.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עבירה לשמה is greater than a מצוה שלא לשמה.

steps.title: Challenge: רב says to do מצוות even not for their own sake
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן בר יצחק from רב's teaching that a person should always do Torah and מצוות even שלא לשמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב יהודה say in the name of רב: A person should always be busy with תורה and מצוות even not for their own sake, because doing it not for its own sake leads to doing it for its own sake?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב נחמן בר יצחק's statement using a famous teaching of רב that values a מצוה שלא לשמה very highly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב says we should do מצוות even with the wrong motive, because that path leads to doing them with the right motive. So a מצוה שלא לשמה has huge value. How can any sin be called greater than it?

keyTerms.meaning: Should be busy with, should occupy himself
Through, out of, as a result of

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Yehuda say in the name of Rav:
A person should always be busy with Torah and מצוות
even not for their own sake,
because from doing it not for its own sake, he comes to do it for its own sake?

steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן בר יצחק's claim that an עבירה לשמה is greater than a מצוה שלא לשמה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב treats a מצוה שלא לשמה as so valuable that one should always do it, since it leads to לשמה. A sin cannot be ranked above that.

steps.title: Correction: a sin for Heaven is equal to a מצוה not for its own sake
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the wording: an עבירה לשמה is like, not greater than, a מצוה שלא לשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: it is like a מצוה not for its own sake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by adjusting רב נחמן בר יצחק's words from 'greater than' to 'equal to.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: This keeps רב's teaching intact, since a מצוה שלא לשמה is not outranked. An עבירה לשמה is still very valuable, but only on the same level. The next step brings a פסוק to prove this equal comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say (the wording should be changed)
Like a מצוה, equal to a מצוה

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not dropping רב נחמן בר יצחק's idea. It only lowers it from 'greater than' to 'equal to.'

phrases.english: Rather, say:
like a מצוה not for its own sake.
phrases.notes: So the statement now reads: a sin for Heaven is equal to a מצוה not for its own sake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by correcting the wording of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the wording of the statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An עבירה לשמה is greater than a מצוה שלא לשמה.
steps.terutzMaskana: An עבירה לשמה is equal to a מצוה שלא לשמה.

steps.title: Proof: יעל is blessed like the women in the tent
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק blesses יעל 'above women in the tent,' meaning the אמהות, putting her act on their level.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'Blessed above women shall יעל be, the wife of חבר the Kenite, above women in the tent she shall be blessed.' Who are the women in the tent? שרה, רבקה, רחל and לאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק to prove the corrected statement: יעל's forbidden act with סיסרא, done for Heaven, is compared to the אמהות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יעל was with סיסרא to save the Jewish people, an עבירה לשמה. The פסוק blesses her alongside the אמהות, which shows her act is ranked equal to theirs. The phrase 'women in the tent' is identified as שרה, רבקה, רחל and לאה.

keyTerms.meaning: The woman who killed סיסרא, the enemy general
The women in the tent, identified as the אמהות

phrases.english: As it is written:
"Blessed above women shall Yael be,
the wife of Chever the Kenite,
above women in the tent she shall be blessed."
Who are the women in the tent?
Sarah, Rivka, Rachel and Leah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the corrected wording from step 7.
steps.raayaObject: The corrected statement that an עבירה לשמה is equal to a מצוה שלא לשמה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שופטים 5:24, blessing יעל like the women in the tent, who are the אמהות.

steps.title: סיסרא was with יעל seven times
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן shows from a פסוק that סיסרא had relations with יעל seven times, so her act was truly a forbidden one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: That wicked man had relations with her seven times at that time, as it says: 'Between her feet he knelt, he fell, he lay, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן proves that יעל really did commit a forbidden act with סיסרא, which is needed for the proof in the previous step to work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof from יעל only works if she actually did an עבירה. רבי יוחנן reads the repeated words in the פסוק, like 'knelt,' 'fell,' 'lay,' as counting seven separate acts.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
That wicked man had relations seven times
at that time,
as it says: "Between her feet he knelt,
phrases.notes: שופטים 5:27. The full פסוק repeats these verbs, and each one counts as another time.

phrases.english: he fell, he lay, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: שֶׁבַע בְּעִילוֹת בָּעַל אוֹתוֹ רָשָׁע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Establishes the fact behind the proof in step 8: יעל's act was a real עבירה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: סיסרא had relations with יעל seven times, learned from the repeated words in שופטים 5:27.

steps.title: Challenge: didn't יעל enjoy it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if יעל got pleasure from the act, how was it purely for Heaven?
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't she getting pleasure from his relations?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions whether יעל's act was really לשמה, since she may have enjoyed it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If יעל got personal pleasure, her act was mixed with a selfish motive. Then why does the פסוק praise her so highly and compare her to the אמהות?

keyTerms.meaning: She was getting pleasure, she benefited

phrases.english: But she was getting pleasure
from his relations?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the act counted in step 9 was really לשמה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that יעל's act was an עבירה לשמה worthy of praise.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Personal pleasure would mean a selfish motive, so the act would not be purely for Heaven.

steps.title: The good of the wicked is bad for the righteous
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that anything good from the wicked is only bad to צדיקים, so יעל did not enjoy it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: All the good of the wicked is nothing but bad for the righteous,
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the challenge: a צדיק like יעל feels no pleasure from anything that comes from a רשע. The next step brings the פסוק that proves this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What a רשע gives, even if it looks like a benefit, is felt as harmful by a צדיק. So יעל took no pleasure from סיסרא, and her act stays fully לשמה.

keyTerms.meaning: Their good, the benefit they give

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
All the good of the wicked
is nothing but bad for the righteous,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כׇּל טוֹבָתָן שֶׁל רְשָׁעִים
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the inner experience of a צדיק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יעל enjoyed the act, so it was not purely לשמה.
steps.terutzMaskana: A צדיק feels the 'good' of a רשע only as bad, so יעל had no pleasure and her act was לשמה.

steps.title: לבן was warned not to say even good things to יעקב
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק warning לבן to speak neither good nor bad to יעקב proves that good from a רשע is bad for a צדיק.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'Guard yourself from speaking to יעקב from good to evil.' Not speaking evil makes sense. But why not good? It must be that his good is bad. Yes, learn this from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for רבי יוחנן's rule from step 11, that good from the wicked is bad for צדיקים. It then explains the proof and accepts it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ה׳ warned לבן not to speak to יעקב 'from good to evil.' Warning him off evil is easy to understand, but there seems to be no reason to stop him from saying good things. The only explanation is that even לבן's 'good' would harm יעקב, and that proves the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Must we not learn from this?

steps.whatToRemember: Good that comes from a רשע counts as bad for a צדיק. That is why יעל did not enjoy what סיסרא did.

phrases.english: As it is stated: "Guard yourself from speaking to Jacob
phrases.notes: בראשית 31:24. ה׳ says this to לבן while he chases יעקב.

phrases.english: from good to evil."
Granted, about evil, that is fine,
but good, why not?
Rather, must we not learn from this:
his good is bad.
Yes, learn from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״הִשָּׁמֶר לְךָ מִדַּבֵּר עִם יַעֲקֹב מִטּוֹב וְעַד רָע״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the פסוק behind רבי יוחנן's answer in step 11.
steps.raayaObject: Good from רשעים is bad for צדיקים
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 31:24, the warning to לבן not to speak to יעקב 'from good to evil'

steps.title: Do תורה and מצוות even not for their own sake
steps.stepSummary: Returning to רב's statement: one should always do תורה and מצוות even שלא לשמה, because it leads to לשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the main teaching. רב יהודה said in the name of רב: A person should always be busy with תורה and מצוות even not for their sake, because from not for their sake he comes to for their sake.
steps.whatsHappening: With the word גופא, the גמרא goes back to look more closely at רב's statement, which was quoted earlier on the daf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב is not praising doing מצוות for the wrong reasons. He is saying you should not hold back from them, because doing them, even with the wrong motive, slowly leads a person to do them for the right reason.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself; going back to look at a statement quoted earlier
Not for their own sake (with another motive)
For their own sake (purely for Heaven)

steps.confusionAlert: רב is not saying שלא לשמה is the goal. It is a starting point that leads to לשמה.

phrases.english: The matter itself:
phrases.notes: We are going back to רב's line that came up earlier on the daf, to look at it more closely.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
A person should always occupy himself with Torah and מצוות
even not for their own sake,
since from doing them not for their own sake, one comes to do them for their own sake.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the יעל discussion and goes back to רב's original statement about שלא לשמה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One should do תורה and מצוות even שלא לשמה, because it leads to לשמה.

steps.title: בלק's offerings earned him רות as a descendant
steps.stepSummary: בלק brought 42 קרבנות only to curse ישראל, yet he was rewarded with רות coming from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because in reward for the forty-two קרבנות that the wicked בלק brought, he merited that רות came from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves רב's point by showing how much reward even a מצוה done שלא לשמה can bring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בלק offered his קרבנות to help בלעם curse the Jewish people, which is about as far from לשמה as possible. Still, ה׳ rewarded him with a great descendant, רות. If even that brings reward, doing מצוות שלא לשמה is clearly worthwhile.

keyTerms.meaning: Balak the wicked, king of מוֹאָב
Ruth, the convert and ancestor of דָּוִד

phrases.english: For in reward for the forty-two offerings
phrases.notes: See במדבר chapter 23. בלק built seven altars three times, with a bull and a ram on each.

phrases.english: that the wicked Balak brought,
he merited that Ruth came from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁבִּשְׂכַר אַרְבָּעִים וּשְׁנַיִם קׇרְבָּנוֹת שֶׁהִקְרִיב בָּלָק הָרָשָׁע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the proof for רב's statement in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: Even a מצוה done שלא לשמה brings great reward
steps.raayaSupportSource: בלק's 42 קרבנות led to רות coming from him

steps.title: רות was עגלון's granddaughter
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא teaches that רות was the granddaughter of עגלון, king of מואב, which ties her back to בלק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: רות was the granddaughter of עגלון, king of מואב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a statement that backs up the claim that רות came from בלק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows the family line: רות came from עגלון, the king of מואב, who came from בלק's royal line. That is how רות counts as בלק's descendant and his reward.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, said:

phrases.aramaic: רוּת, בַּת בְּנוֹ שֶׁל עֶגְלוֹן מֶלֶךְ מוֹאָב הָיְתָה.
phrases.english: Ruth was the granddaughter of Eglon, king of Moab.
phrases.notes: This links רות back to בלק, since עגלון came from בלק's line of מואב kings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 14 by showing the family link from בלק to רות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רות was the granddaughter of עגלון מלך מואב.

steps.title: No reward is lost, even for refined speech: the case of מואב
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן asks for the source that ה׳ rewards even refined speech, and starts with the older daughter of לוט, who named her son מואב. Her descendants were only protected from war.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: How do we know ה׳ does not hold back even the reward for refined speech? The older daughter named her son מואב, and ה׳ told משה, 'Do not besiege מואב or fight them in war.' War is forbidden, but harassing them is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new, related teaching about reward. It starts with the first half of a comparison between לוט's two daughters, and the second half comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The older daughter openly named her son מואב, a name that points to where he came from. Because of that, her descendants got only partial protection: ישראל could not wage war on them, but could still harass them.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן שֶׁאֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְקַפֵּחַ
phrases.english: From where do we know that the Holy One, Blessed be He, does not withhold
even the reward for refined speech?
For the older daughter, who named him Moab,
phrases.notes: These are לוט's daughters. The name מואב sounds like 'from father,' which openly points to how he was born.

phrases.english: the Merciful One said to him:

phrases.aramaic: ״אַל תָּצַר אֶת מוֹאָב וְאַל תִּתְגָּר בָם מִלְחָמָה״.
phrases.english: "Do not besiege Moab, nor contend with them in war."
It is war that is not allowed,
but harassing them, they could harass them.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנַּיִן שֶׁאֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְקַפֵּחַ אֲפִילּוּ שְׂכַר שִׂיחָה נָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching about reward that also involves מואב, following the בלק and רות discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳ does not withhold even the reward for refined speech. This step shows the lesser protection given to מואב.

steps.title: בן עמי's descendants got full protection
steps.stepSummary: The younger daughter named her son בן עמי, a modest name, so her descendants (עמון) may not even be harassed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the younger daughter named him בן עמי, and ה׳ said, 'Do not harass them, nor fight them.' Even harassing them is not allowed at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the comparison and completes רבי יוחנן's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The younger daughter chose a modest name, בן עמי ('son of my people'), that did not mention her father. In reward, her descendants got full protection, with not even harassment allowed. The difference between the two nations shows that ה׳ rewards even refined speech.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Son of my people,' father of עַמּוֹן

steps.whatToRemember: One modest word choice earned a whole nation lasting protection. ה׳ does not hold back reward even for refined speech.

phrases.english: But the younger daughter, who named him Ben Ammi,
He said to him:
"Do not harass them, nor contend with them."
phrases.notes: דברים 2:19. This one leaves out the word 'war,' so the ban covers everything.

phrases.english: Even harassing, you may not harass them at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the comparison started in step 16.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 2:19 compared with דברים 2:9: עמון gets full protection, while מואב gets only protection from war

steps.title: Always be first to do a מצוה, as the older daughter went first
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבין quotes רבי יהושע בן קרחה: a person should always rush to do a מצוה. He starts to prove it from the one night the older daughter of לוט went before the younger.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבין said that רבי יהושע בן קרחה said: A person should always be the first to do a מצוה. For as a reward for the one night that the older daughter acted before the younger one... (the reward is described on the next amud).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching: always hurry to be first when doing a מצוה. It begins proving this from the older daughter of לוט, and it is setting up the reward she got, which comes in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps were about reward for clean, modest speech, where the younger daughter came out ahead. Now the focus switches to being first. The older daughter acted one night before her sister, and she is about to be rewarded just for going first.

keyTerms.meaning: Should come first, should hurry ahead
A matter of a מצוה, a good deed

steps.confusionAlert: Don't let the order fool you. In the last step the younger daughter got the better reward for her modest naming. Here the older one is rewarded for a different thing, being first. The two rewards are for two separate good points.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Avin said
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha said:
A person should always be first
to a matter of a מצוה,
for in reward for one night
that the older one went before the younger,
phrases.notes: These are the two daughters of לוט. The sentence isn't finished; the reward comes on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Stays with the daughters of לוט from steps 16-17, but moves from the reward for modest speech to a new idea, the reward for being first to do a מצוה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person should always hurry to be first in doing a מצוה. This is learned from the reward the older daughter of לוט received for acting one night before her sister.
